title: Site stardust: stateless particles advected by the ground's flow texture, rendered to a half-res layer, blurred by the clouds' accumulated opacity (raymarch-driven DoF), composited behind the nebula
first: Map: F:/Projects/CultLib/docs/cultmath-interval-ground-cut.md, 'Stardust', 'Depth of field driven by the raymarch', 'Budget', D4, D9, D10. Re-pin base to main after site-ground lands. The composite slot site-ground left in the resolve is where this cut plugs in; do not restructure the resolve.

Aetheria reference, read once, copy nothing: Compute/Stardust/Stardust.compute:118-147 (grid cell -> hashed spawn, lifetime = frac(time/period + hash), position -= flow * lifetime * period, size = parabola(lifetime, 2), colour from a hue ramp x nebula tint); Stardust.shader:49-86 (billboard from quadPoints by SV_VertexID/SV_InstanceID, powerPulse falloff, distance exponents); CustomDoF/DepthOfField.hlsl:29-32 (CoC read from a raymarch output), :150-201 (disk gather weighted by CoC), :217-242 (combine). The web version is far smaller: no distance exponents (the slab is thin), no shadow pass, no near/far split.

Particles are stateless: no buffers are updated. One static 6-vertex quad VBO; drawArraysInstanced with count N; the vertex shader derives everything from gl_InstanceID, time and the flow texture (vertex texture fetch is standard in WebGL2): cell = (id mod G, id / G) over the slab mid-plane; hashes via cultmath_pcg3d (the vendored CultMath.glsl is concatenated before the vertex source too) for spawn jitter, lifetime offset, size and brightness; lifetime = fract(t / PERIOD_P + offset); position = spawn - flow(spawn uv) * lifetime * PERIOD_P; size = base * parabola(lifetime, 2); colour = hue at the screen position (from the flow texture's channels, the same mix as the clouds) * brightness. Reduced motion freezes t as site-ground does.

Stardust layer: half-resolution RGBA16F target, cleared each frame, additive blend, powerPulse falloff in the fragment shader; N = 16384 desktop, 4096 phone; the controller scales N with S (N halves when S halves) and the layer follows dpr.

DoF: in the resolve's composite slot, read opacity = 1 - T from the reprojected, clamped history (not the current frame) and gather the stardust layer with an 8-tap Poisson disk of radius RMAX * opacity in layer texels (RMAX ~ 12 px at dpr 1, scaled by dpr); weight taps by a soft disk; composite out = ground + clouds + stardust_blurred * T, then the luminance clamp. All stardust is behind the whole cloud layer (D9).

Debug flags: ?ground=debug-stardust writes the stardust layer alone; ?ground=debug-coc writes opacity into red. Prove in the browser pane: the stardust and the clouds move together (with ?ground=debug-mv from site-ground and the particle velocity written in green under ?ground=debug-stardust-v, the two directions agree within 5 degrees at 64 sampled pixels where |flow| is above a threshold); luminance clamp still holds after the composite; GPU ms per pass (stardust layer, gather) with the timer query at desktop and at the mobile preset's pixel count; the full-stack total against the budget table; the unfinished-ray fraction unchanged by this cut.

Budget contract (map, 'Budget'): the stardust layer plus the gather cost no more than a quarter of the march at the same S; if the measurement says otherwise, the gather drops to 4 taps before N drops, and the report says which. Stardust is never cut before the clouds' S on the ladder.
keeps_moves: site-ground's flow texture, march, TAA, readback and token writer: untouched; the stardust reads the flow texture and the hue mix the same way the clouds do.
The sampled wash now includes the stardust in its 8x8 readback by construction (it samples the final frame); nothing changes in the writer.
The budget controller gains one scaled quantity (N) and no new state; the ladder order is unchanged.
adds: site/quartz/static/ground/stardust.vert.glsl and stardust.frag.glsl: the instanced billboard and the powerPulse sprite.
ground.js: the stardust pass (one VBO, one program, drawArraysInstanced), the half-res layer, N in the controller, the gather in the resolve's composite slot, the two debug flags.
taa.frag.glsl: the composite slot filled: opacity from history, the 8-tap gather, out = ground + clouds + stardust_blurred * T.
docs/brand-design-language.md: two sentences under the ground shader paragraph: the stardust and the DoF, and that they read the same flow and hue as the nebula.

authority_map.owner: ground.js owns the stardust pass and the DoF gather; the flow texture (site-ground) owns the particles' motion; the TAA history owns the opacity the DoF reads; the nebula input tokens own the particles' hue through the same mix as the clouds.
inputs: the flow texture and the hue mix (site-ground)
time, N and dpr from the controller; gl_InstanceID
outputs: a half-res stardust layer per frame
the composite with stardust blurred by cloud opacity behind the nebula, still under the luminance clamp
derived_state: every particle's position, lifetime, size and colour are derived from gl_InstanceID, time and the flow texture each frame; nothing is stored or updated
N is derived from S by the controller; the layer size from dpr
the blur radius is derived from the accumulated opacity; there is no second CoC source
forbidden_writers: no particle buffer update, transform feedback or CPU-side particle state
no second flow function or hue mix; the vertex shader samples the flow texture
no colour literal; no per-depth transmittance; no second march
no new controller state beyond N; the ladder order is not changed
no change to the readback or the token writer
shared_paths: clouds and stardust read one flow texture and one hue mix, so they move and colour as one
the one resolve pass composites ground, clouds and stardust and applies the one luminance clamp
the one controller scales S, N and dpr together
authority_map.deletion_line: Nothing is deleted. The addition is two small shaders, one pass and one gather; it buys the stardust and the DoF the operator named, and it must prove it fits the same budget.
